feature_name: Capture and submit a queued page
scope: Proposed procedure-only replacement for existing case EXT-F-2002-T01. No inventory status, cells, control status, runtime evidence, or product behavior is changed or claimed.

proposed_changes.title: Capture, continue, paste, retry, and resolve owned queued sources

control_link_exceptions.reason: The current PasteRow source renders a textarea and Submit paste but no cancel-editor control. Do not infer an editor-cancel action from navigation or invent a new UI action; reconcile this inventory control against the source before assigning a runtime verdict.

The source offers capture-level grouping and a capture-level queue filter, not a per-source capture-intensity picker. The linked step checks the source-present filter behavior only and makes no claim that it changes a queued item's capture intensity.

guest.reason: Tasks tab audience is signed-in; canAccessSidepanelTab returns viewer.signedIn for signed-in tabs, and App gates both its trigger and content through canAccess('tasks'). EXT-F-2002-T01 is not the guest denial case.

member.reason: Tasks is available to signed-in viewers without an admin predicate; feature inventory already marks member applicable. Queue and writes still require actual member role and explicitly selected device organization.

admin.reason: Tasks is available to signed-in viewers; feature inventory already marks admin applicable. Use an actual admin principal and explicitly selected device organization.

preconditions: For each member and admin run, use a separate, real signed-in profile and an explicitly selected device organization. Capture the principal role and organization in the receipt; do not use the active organization as a list filter or infer member access from admin access.

Complete the resource permit and full build receipt required by docs/stabilization/PLAN.md § Build and reload contract. Use the approved receipt-bound extension artifact, verify loaded extension identity and source/tree hashes, reopen the actual side panel, and reload the controlled target pages after any applicable extension reload. Record no secrets.

Use only campaign-owned disposable queued sources in the selected organization, with a known URL and known queue bucket. Prepare distinct sources for L1, L2, L3 continuation, L3 expect-thin, L3 cancel, L4 paste, retry, and each terminal verdict branch. If the required owned source or a naturally qualifying thin response is unavailable, leave that branch unverified; do not repurpose personal/organization records or fabricate backend responses.
Keep one owned ordinary page open in the disposable profile for the source-link check. Do not use an everyday browsing profile. Record fixture identifiers only, not page text or credential data.
steps: In each role profile, open the actual side panel → Tasks. Confirm the owned fixture rows and their known levels. Open the filter popover, include only one capture-level bucket, then exclude it; repeat for a second bucket. Switch the grouping toggle between capture level and project, then clear filters. Confirm rows are filtered/grouped and return to the original full queue. This checks the source-present filter/group controls, not a change to an item's level. [C08]

For the owned L1 source and then the owned L2 source, click its visible Run/Capture action while its URL is not already the active tab. Observe loading/error/success state and queue refresh. For L2, also observe page settling/scroll behavior on the controlled page. Record the actual terminal UI result; success and thin are distinct outcomes, and an explicit error is not a pass. [C01, C05, C13]

For the owned L3 user-gated source, click Trigger/Capture this tab. Confirm the target page becomes active and the in-page Matrx overlay appears. On this fixture, first click Cancel and confirm the overlay closes while the queued source remains available. On a separate L3 fixture, trigger again, complete the page gate yourself, and click Capture page in the overlay or Go in the side panel; wait for capture submission and inspect the row status. [C02, C04, C11]

On a separate owned L3 source, trigger the overlay and click Expect thin content. If the response is thin, verify the source is resolved as accepted and the page tab is closed; if it is not thin, record that the auto-accept-thin branch was not exercised. Do not induce a thin response by mutating network/backend behavior. [C03]
On the controlled ordinary page, click the queued source URL and confirm it opens that source in a separate browser tab. Return to Tasks. [C12]

For the owned L4 source, enter a short synthetic marker string into the paste field and submit it. Observe success/error and whether the field clears; verify the queue refresh. On another L4 source, leave the editor without submitting and verify there was no content submission. Do not claim a cancel control exists; C10 is separately flagged as unmatched in current source. [C09]

For a source with a prior capture attempt, open Resolve and verify Retry from scratch is available; select it and observe the queue refresh/requeue. Separately, if a capture action produces a real recoverable error on an owned fixture, click the row's Run/Trigger action again and observe whether a new attempt starts. If no error occurs, leave retry-after-error coverage unverified. [C05, C13, C17]

Using distinct owned sources, open Resolve and exercise This is the whole page, Page is gated, and Page is dead / 404 one at a time; use Retry from scratch only on a source with a previous attempt. Observe pending state, success/error feedback, queue refresh, and whether terminal sources leave the queue while Retry requeues. Do not choose a terminal verdict for non-disposable sources. [C06, C14, C15, C16, C17]

Repeat the applicable warm procedure for each role after the exact extension reload/reopen and controlled-page reload required by PLAN.md. Compare observed result and role-specific access; do not reuse a prior run's result as evidence for the other role.
expected: Tasks appears for signed-in member and admin profiles. Queue access, fixture ownership and writes are evaluated separately for each principal under its explicitly selected organization. Guest access is covered only by the existing EXT-F-2002 guest/access case, not this case.

Capture-level filter inclusion/exclusion and grouping visibly alter which rows are shown or how they are grouped; clearing filters restores the full queue. The UI does not alter the underlying source's assigned capture level through these controls.

L1/L2 actions visibly enter their loading phases and either show a successful/thin result followed by queue refresh or a specific recoverable error. A created/reused tab follows actual source behavior; do not assert an unverified server or parser outcome as fixed.

L3 Trigger opens the user-gate overlay and waits for an explicit person action. Cancel removes the overlay and clears the local in-progress state without submitting capture or removing the queued source. Capture page/Go removes the overlay and submits the currently loaded page; a successful thin result exposes its verdict card, while errors remain visible.

Expect thin content only auto-applies accept_as_is when the returned capture is thin. A non-thin response does not prove the conditional accept branch; unavailable fixture behavior remains unverified. The overlay action closes its tab after its capture path completes.
The source URL link opens its URL in a separate tab; the Tasks side panel and source row remain available.

Paste submission with non-empty content sends trimmed text for that queued source, shows success or a specific error, and clears the local paste value only after success. Empty content cannot be submitted. There is no source-backed cancel-editor control to assert for C10.

Resolve → Retry is offered only after at least one attempted level. A successful retry action requeues the source and it is visible after refresh; terminal verdicts mark completion and the source leaves the queue after refresh. Failures remain visible as errors and preserve a recoverable path.

Warm and reload observations are recorded independently for member and admin. Only source-backed, visibly observed behavior is eligible for later runtime verdict assignment; this proposed procedure itself leaves all inventory cells and evidence states unchanged.

evidence.finding: Procedures require resource admission and a receipt binding source/dirty hash, lock/output hashes, WXT mode, runtime ID, Chrome/profile, auth/role/org, permissions, backend identity and fixture IDs; extension reload/reopen and controlled target-tab reload are required where applicable. Warm and reloaded runs are distinct.
Case procedures need concrete reproduction, controlled data prerequisites, source-backed applicability, and no pass verdict from source reading.

EXT-F-2002 defines one broad case, EXT-F-2002-T01, existing control IDs C01-C17 except C07, modes member/admin, and guest/member/admin feature applicability. Case controls and useful reproduction details are currently absent/generic.
Tasks audience is signed-in; access returns signedIn for signed-in tabs.
Both Tasks navigation trigger and mounted Tasks content are gated by canAccess('tasks').

Source maps queue actions to the user-gate message handler, automated capture and L3 overlay/Go/expect-thin flows, cancel/pre-decided verdicts, HTML/media submission and thin verdict card, paste submit, retry/terminal resolution, source links, and visible row controls.
The L3 overlay is mounted in the target tab and exposes Cancel, Expect thin content, Capture page, Gated and 404/dead controls.
Queue buckets map to levels; current level sections include automated, user-gated, gated-login, manual paste and low-value; this supports fixture selection by known bucket.
Toolbar implements group-by-capture-level and a capture-level filter group. This does not expose a per-item intensity picker.
Resolve options are accept_as_is, content_mismatch, gated, dead_link, ignored and retry; retry is shown only after a prior attempt.

limits: This is source-only procedure design. No browser, build, test, backend, or live fixture was exercised; member/admin access and all runtime outcomes remain unverified.

C10 is not represented by a current cancel control in PasteRow. C08's inventory description overstates the current filter/group UI as a per-source intensity picker. The proposal exposes both mismatches instead of inventing behaviors.

The feature spans organization-scoped backend writes and terminal verdicts. Only campaign-owned disposable fixture sources are safe for execution; fixture creation and cleanup ownership must be established outside this procedure before a native run.
